question: Should OpenClaw sponsor this experimental core Claw update-plan contract, including its versioned CLI/JSON surface and capability-escalation consent model, as the basis for the stacked lifecycle work?
rationale: The patch is a coherent read-only implementation, but deciding whether grouped Claw lifecycle ownership and future consent semantics belong in core is a maintainer product and architecture choice rather than a mechanical repair.

options.title: Sponsor the read-only planner
options.body: Approve this experimental planning contract after its diagnostics base is ready, while requiring the downstream apply path to enforce distinct consent for escalations.

options.title: Narrow the core surface
options.body: Retain only generic lifecycle primitives in core and move grouped update UX or policy to an extension-facing owner.

options.title: Defer pending RFC direction
options.body: Pause this stacked slice until the RFC settles the intended core ownership, upgrade policy, and consent UX.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the read-only planner
recommendation.body: Approve this experimental planning contract after its diagnostics base is ready, while requiring the downstream apply path to enforce distinct consent for escalations.

likelyOwner.reason: He is assigned and has already defined the key planner-safety requirements in review.
